A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching title, authors, methods and core experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies can be identified without preventing comparison of the revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original conformal-prediction experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet and ImageNet variants, including calibration, distribution-shift and few-shot analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds MetaCLIP evaluations, broader few-shot results and additional sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same LAC, APS, RAPS, temperature-scaling, linear-probing and existing few-shot adaptation procedures. Evaluating additional pretrained models does not introduce an algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: Few-shot evaluation expands beyond ImageNet and its variants to ten additional datasets: SUN397, FGVCAircraft, EuroSAT, StanfordCars, Food101, OxfordPets, Flowers102, Caltech101, DTD and UCF101. This substantially broadens represented scenes, fine-grained objects, textures, land-cover and action categories. The original dataset coverage remains.

E2.justification: MetaCLIP joins the general and calibration comparisons. Table 1 also adds MetaCLIP and DINO-S to the supervised-ViT comparison; DINO-S already appeared elsewhere in v1. The three CP methods and the ZS, ZSLP, CLAP, CoOp and KgCoOp few-shot comparator set remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 4-shot setting alongside 16 shots and changes Table 3's ID aggregation from ImageNet alone to an average over 11 datasets. Table 1 additionally includes ViT-S through DINO-S, broadening the previously ViT-B comparison. Existing CP hyperparameters and the 16-shot OOD protocol are retained.

E4.justification: Temperature sensitivity, previously examined on ImageNet, is extended across CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 in v2 Figures 10–13. New sample-level set-size distributions compare supervised ViT with MetaCLIP and DINO-S, and Tables 10–11 support a 4-versus-16-shot sensitivity analysis. Together these substantially expand the supplementary checks; the existing domain-shift analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 1 already contains regression shading and correlation statistics in v1. Neither version provides run counts, seeds or specified significance tests, and v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds MetaCLIP scores and extensive 4-shot and 16-shot results, and revises Figure 1 correlations and ImageNet ECE curves. Table 3's ID zero-shot APS size changes from 10.07 to 6.98 under different dataset aggregation, not as a same-setting improvement. OOD values are retained. New Table 11 conflicts with retained Table 9 on some ImageNet entries, including CoOp APS size 5.27 versus 6.32, without explaining the difference.

T1.justification: The CP definitions, scoring functions, coverage assumptions, RAPS accuracy argument and Appendix A metric equations remain substantively unchanged. Notation edits and additional pointers to existing coverage guarantees do not add mathematical results or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 withdraws the headline claim that adapters are generally preferable to prompt learning, removing it from the abstract, introduction observation (vi) and conclusion. It instead emphasizes better conformalization after few-shot adaptation on ID data, with marginal OOD gains. This materially revises a principal practical recommendation; the other central findings remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.2.4 now interprets the expanded ID results as slightly favoring prompt learning while emphasizing limited OOD gains. v2 also develops v1's acknowledgment of unequal training-data amounts into an explicit limitation of the supervised/foundation-model comparison. Section 2 clarifies that transfer learning need not itself alter marginal coverage guarantees.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same Adam learning rate, patience, PyTorch/TorchCP implementation, RAPS parameters and coverage levels. No additional hardware, runtime, checkpoint or code/data-access instructions are supplied. The added evaluation budgets are protocol changes rather than expanded implementation documentation.

R1.justification: References are added for the new datasets, MetaCLIP and Tip-Adapter, with limited clarification of the research gap concerning efficiency and conditional coverage. The central positioning remains unchanged. Tip-Adapter is cited for context but is not added to the reported comparator set.

P1.justification: v2 polishes and condenses prose, rewrites the few-shot discussion and shortens the conclusion. It introduces Appendix E on set-size analysis, moving the former Appendices E and F to F and G. The main section structure and experimental narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The appendix gains extensive CIFAR temperature-plot grids, two set-size histograms and two detailed few-shot tables. Existing tables gain model rows, and Figure 1 axes and calibration-plot legends/scales are revised. Earlier Figures 10–14 are retained as Figures 14–18; their relocation is distinct from the genuinely new displays.

improvement.justification: The broader few-shot evidence supports replacing v1's ImageNet-based adapter recommendation with more qualified ID/OOD claims. Additional calibration checks and a more explicit pretraining-scale limitation also strengthen the paper. The net improvement is limited by newly introduced reporting inconsistencies, notably conflicting ImageNet results in Tables 9 and 11 and the mixing of MetaCLIP MCCC values with retained coverage-gap values in Tables 4–6.
